question: Is any repair shop an outlier on cost? Read the claim notes for context too.

input.sql: select c.repair_shop_id, r.name, r.network_status, r.state, count(*) n, round(avg(p.paid),0) avg_paid from claims c join repair_shops r using(repair_shop_id) left join (select claim_id, sum(amount) paid from claim_payments group by 1) p using(claim_id) where c.cause in ('collision','glass','storm') group by all order by avg_paid desc limit 12

report.interpretation: I read 'cost' as the average paid per motor collision, glass and storm claim by repair shop. Paid is the sum of claim_payments. I excluded the 198 duplicate rows from the 'reload-2026-03-14' batch. I only compared shops with at least 30 claims. All loss dates are included, and the latest weeks are incomplete because claims are reported late.
report.answer: Yes. RS-010 Patton Panel & Paint (VIC, non-preferred) is the outlier. It averages $9,157 per claim across 235 claims, the highest of any shop with 30 or more claims. The next shops are RS-004 at $8,181 and RS-006 at $7,451. The gap is driven by collision claims, which average $11,984 at RS-010. The problem is recent and concentrated. Since April 2026 (quarters from Q2 2026), RS-010 collisions run at about $17–18k, against about $6.6–10.5k before. Adjuster ADJ-012 (Becky Crane, VIC & TAS) handles 46% of the shop's claims. Her 47 RS-010 collision claims since April 2026 average $18,538, against $8,419 for other VIC/TAS collisions in the same period. Her collisions at other shops are normal at about $7.2k. So the pattern is specific to the shop and adjuster pairing. This is evidence for review, not a finding of wrongdoing. The claim notes are generic templates ('rear-ended at traffic lights', 'reversed into a bollard') and don't explain the higher costs. Six RS-010 storm claims have 'hail dents' notes, but none of their loss dates fall in a recorded hail event in the weather data. Broker-sold policies show the highest cost at RS-010 since April ($15,749 across 47 claims, against about $9–10k for direct and online). I recommend a referral to SIU or the fraud team for invoice and assessment review.
report.answer_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) pp from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'reload%' group by 1) select c.repair_shop_id, r.name, r.network_status, count(*) n, round(avg(pp),0) avg_paid from claims c join repair_shops r using(repair_shop_id) left join p using(claim_id) where cause in ('collision','glass','storm') group by 1,2,3 having count(*)>=30 order by avg_paid desc limit 1

findings.claim: RS-010 has the highest average paid per claim of shops with 30 or more claims, with RS-004 and RS-006 behind it.
findings.evidence_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) pp from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'reload%' group by 1) select c.repair_shop_id, count(*) n, round(avg(pp),0) avg_paid from claims c join repair_shops r using(repair_shop_id) left join p using(claim_id) where cause in ('collision','glass','storm') group by 1 having count(*)>=30 order by avg_paid desc limit 3

findings.claim: RS-010 collision costs jumped from Q2 2026. ADJ-012's collisions at RS-010 since April 2026 average 2.2 times those of other VIC/TAS collisions.
findings.evidence_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) pp from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'reload%' group by 1) select 'RS-010 ADJ-012 collisions since Apr 2026' grp, count(*) n, round(avg(pp),0) avg_paid from claims c left join p using(claim_id) where cause='collision' and repair_shop_id='RS-010' and adjuster_id='ADJ-012' and loss_date>='2026-04-01' union all select 'Other VIC/TAS collisions since Apr 2026', count(*), round(avg(pp),0) from claims c left join p using(claim_id) where cause='collision' and state in ('VIC','TAS') and loss_date>='2026-04-01' and not (repair_shop_id='RS-010' and adjuster_id='ADJ-012')

data_quality_issues.issue: 198 duplicate payment rows were loaded in the out-of-batch 'reload-2026-03-14' load (payments from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13).
data_quality_issues.impact: Including them overstates paid amounts. RS-010 would show $9,323 instead of $9,157. I excluded them.

data_quality_issues.issue: Claim notes are generic templates and don't match the loss facts in some cases, for example hail notes with no recorded hail event.
data_quality_issues.impact: The notes give little context for cost, so I haven't relied on them.
